sources.ref: NTA, JEE (Main) 2026 Session 2, B.E./B.Tech question paper 'B Tech 2nd Apr 2026 Shift 1' (English)
NTA, JEE (Main) 2026 Session 2 final answer key of B.E./B.Tech on which result compiled, Exam Date 02.04.2026, Shift First (page 1)

notes: Previous-year questions from NTA's JEE (Main) 2026 paper of 2 April 2026, Shift 1 (B.E./B.Tech), ingested with pyq-ingest. Stems, options, statements and list items keep NTA's English wording exactly; NTA published this paper in English only, so the Hindi is our translation (hi_source: translation) and must be reviewed as such. Answers are NTA's final key (result-compiled, Session 2); our own solutions reach the same answer for every question in this file. Question ids 9001 and up mark ingested PYQs.

stem.en: $t_{100\%}$ is the time required for the $100\%$ completion of the reaction while $t_{1/2}$ is the time required for $50\%$ of the reaction to be completed. Which of the following option correctly represents the relation between $t_{100\%}$ and $t_{1/2}$ for zero and first order reactions respectively ?
stem.hi: $t_{100\%}$ अभिक्रिया के $100\%$ पूर्ण होने में लगा समय है, जबकि $t_{1/2}$ अभिक्रिया के $50\%$ पूर्ण होने में लगा समय है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विकल्प शून्य और प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रियाओं के लिए क्रमशः $t_{100\%}$ और $t_{1/2}$ के बीच संबंध को सही दर्शाता है ?

feynman.en: A zero order reaction uses reactant at a steady rate, so finishing takes exactly twice as long as getting halfway. A first order reaction halves again and again and never quite finishes.
feynman.hi: शून्य कोटि की अभिक्रिया अभिकारक को स्थिर दर से खर्च करती है, अतः पूर्ण होने में आधे तक पहुँचने का ठीक दोगुना समय लगता है। प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया बार-बार आधी होती है और कभी पूरी नहीं होती।

steps.en: First order: $t=\frac1k\ln\frac{[A]_0}{[A]}$ grows without bound as $[A] \to 0$, written in the option as $(t_{1/2})^{\infty}$.
steps.hi: प्रथम कोटि: $t=\frac1k\ln\frac{[A]_0}{[A]}$, $[A] \to 0$ पर असीमित बढ़ता है, जिसे विकल्प में $(t_{1/2})^{\infty}$ लिखा गया है।
